lines.caption: This is a tour of pull request 13, which gives every push to a pull request an independent code review in CI.
It has three parts: what this PR adds, how it was built and verified, and what comes later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
It starts when you push. With no trailer the review fixes what it finds; with Review: suggest it only suggests.
lines.say: It starts when you push. With no trailer, the review fixes what it finds. With a review suggest trailer, it only suggests.

lines.caption: The plan step picks the mode and reviews only the commits since the last review.
Claude runs the built-in code review at xhigh, and a fresh agent tries to disprove each finding.
lines.say: Claude runs the built-in code review at extra high, and a fresh agent tries to disprove each finding.

lines.caption: The findings and the fix are saved as an artifact for the next job.
A second job, which holds the push token, pushes the confirmed fixes as one claude[bot] commit.
lines.say: A second job, which holds the push token, pushes the confirmed fixes as one Claude bot commit.

lines.caption: Findings that weren't pushed become one-click suggested changes on the PR.
Then it writes the review section of the PR comment, and goes red only on medium or high findings.
You decide what's next: pull the fix, commit a suggestion, accept a finding, or merge.
Until now, code was reviewed in the same session that wrote it. Now CI reviews exactly what was pushed, with no memory of it.
The reviewer never holds a token that can push. A separate job checks its edit and pushes it.
Step one: any push from this repo starts it. Pull requests from forks are skipped, since they get no secrets.
Step two waits for an earlier run's report, and skips a push that only changed the explainer pages.
Step three: only findings the second agent confirms count, and only those are fixed.
The bot's commit gets its own follow-up review, which only reports, so the loop ends there.
The report keeps every finding numbered across the whole pull request.
A red review never blocks the merge. The decision stays yours.
Trailers on the head commit pick the mode, and Review-accept closes findings you keep on purpose.
lines.say: Trailers on the head commit pick the mode, and a review accept trailer closes findings you keep on purpose.

lines.caption: The state lives in a hidden line of the PR comment, so nothing else needs storing.
The fix never touches the workflows, the review scripts, or the files the action resets.
Only medium or high findings fail the job, and the report job shouldn't be re-run on its own.
The PR adds three scripts and two jobs, and updates the repo's instructions and the explainer skill.
To stop the pushes, delete the push token secret. Fixes then fall back to suggestions.
Part 2. How it was built and verified.
It builds on Anthropic's GitHub Action, the built-in code review skill, and the PR comment from issue 9.
Structured findings worked with the owner's token, and no GitHub App was needed.
A planted search bug, pushed plainly, came back fixed by the bot, and the follow-up only reported.
A planted use-after-free, pushed in suggest mode, turned the job red until the owner committed the suggestion.
An empty commit forced a review of the whole pull request, which took twenty minutes.
An explainer-only push skipped the review, the comment kept one section, and accepted findings stopped failing it.
The report was also replayed locally after each hand change, and the minutes were measured from the API.
A pull request from a fork wasn't tried.
A fresh local agent reviewed the final diff. It found four issues: one fixed here, three left open.
CI's own review ran on every push and reported 230 findings; the bot fixed 88 of them.
lines.say: The C I review itself ran on every push and reported 230 findings; the bot fixed 88 of them.

lines.caption: It never converged on its own scripts, so the loop was stopped by hand, and a few gaps are kept on purpose.
A pull request from a cloud agent, and one that starts from main, can only be checked after the merge.
Part 3. What comes later.
In issue 7, cloud agents open pull requests, this review and a verify job check them, and you merge.
Its minutes budget now uses the numbers measured here: about eleven minutes for a small push.
That's the tour: every push now gets a fresh, independent review, fixed or suggested, and reported in one place.
